newsitem.title: USA: Stephanopoulos says he may one day run for office.
newsitem.headline: Stephanopoulos says he may one day run for office.

text.p: White House adviser George Stephanopoulos, who is leaving the Clinton administration for a university teaching job, said on Wednesday he may run for political office some day.

"It's something I want to think about," he told a news conference at Columbia University, where he will teach political science next year. Asked if he had political aspirations, he said, "I certainly haven't ruled it out."
In addition to teaching, Stephanopoulos, 35, said he planned to work in television and write a book after he leaves his White House job.
President Bill Clinton said in a statement that "no one has rendered me better advice or given more loyal service to this nation than George Stephanopoulos."

"His work here at the White House is evidence of his deep respect for our country, its system of government and its people. He cannot be replaced," he said in remarks read to reporters by White House spokesman Mike McCurry.
"George will undoubtedly be a great teacher at Columbia. His boundless intellectual curiosity will be put to good use shaping the leadership of the future," Clinton said.

McCurry joked that Clinton cut out of a draft statement a suggestion from women staffers that he say that Stephanopoulos was now "the most eligible studmuffin in New York" now that John Kennedy Jr had married.

At Columbia, where he earned an undergraduate degree in political science in 1982, Stephanopoulos will be a visiting professor for two years, teaching seminars, delivering lectures and holding informal "town meetings" with students. He will focus on politics, policy, the press and the presidency, he said.

After helping in Clinton's 1992 campaign, Stephanopoulos became White House communications director and briefly served as the president's spokesman. As senior adviser behind the scenes, he has been a Clinton confidant and worked closely with members of Congress.
Stephanopoulos' boyish good looks also made him a bit of a celebrity. Asked by a reporter how he felt about becoming one of New York City's most eligible bachelors, he laughed and refused to comment.
